boundary_note: Bounded first pass in the complete five-engagement frozen Burnside campaign. Opening populations and replacement boundaries are unresolved. NPS and an interested retrospective history supply attributed claims only; no predictors or causal command scores are admitted.

claims.value: The frozen table supplies US 7,500 and CS 3,000. The NPS narrative describes 7,500 Union men landing on February 7, whereas its structured table calls the numbers forces engaged.
claims.rationale: The numerical counts remain imported estimates. A landing population and the subsequent assault population are not automatically identical; the table does not establish a common opening boundary.

citations.quote: Burnside landed 7,500 men on the southwestern side of Roanoke Island

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched opening populations. The existing imported numerical estimates keep their baseline role but are not newly validated as opening counts. Retrospective formations, gun crews, garrisons, prisoners and troops engaged must not be interchanged.

claims.value: NPS describes Confederate forts on the narrow waist of Roanoke Island and a Union landing on its southwestern side.
claims.rationale: Retain these attributed locations without a measured terrain advantage or verified map.

citations.quote: the southwestern side of Roanoke Island
the Confederate forts on the narrow waist of the island

claims.value: Woodbury says rain and wind interrupted the planned February 6 movement, with the fleet anchoring during a gale; movement resumed under better conditions on the 7th.
claims.rationale: A retrospective account of approach conditions, not quantified readiness or a validated causal contribution. This preceding day is context outside the frozen February 7–8 interval.

claims.value: Woodbury describes an escaped enslaved youth identified as Tom providing Burnside information about island defenses and a landing place at Ashby’s Harbor.
claims.rationale: Attributed to a non-eyewitness history; no original interview or message was inspected. The author’s praise does not establish the accuracy or causal value of every reported statement.

claims.rationale: An attributed operational task preceding the battle, not an inspected original order or a quantified strategic objective.

claims.value: NPS identifies Shaw as the Confederate commander on the field who surrendered, despite listing Wise as the principal Confederate commander.
claims.rationale: Principal listing and exercised field authority remain distinct. Burnside’s landing and gunboat support also do not imply sole credit for the outcome.

citations.quote: the Confederate commander on the field, Col. H.M. Shaw, surrendered about 2,500 soldiers and 32 guns.

claims.value: The frozen row and live NPS page record a Union victory.
claims.rationale: Same source family, not independent corroboration or a causal effect. Retain the frozen engagement interval and do not add a separate score for later occupation or campaign consequences.

claims.value: The frozen casualty record separates US 37 killed, 214 wounded and 13 missing from CS 23 killed, 58 wounded, 62 missing and 2,500 captured. NPS also says the Confederates surrendered after losing fewer than 100 men.
claims.rationale: The narrative phrase must not replace the broad casualty aggregate or erase missing/captured categories. Prisoners and the opening Confederate population are not interchangeable; these remain unadjudicated source counts.

open_questions: Original orders, personnel returns, contemporary intelligence and source disputes remain deferred after the bounded shared-history follow-up. OCR has not been checked against print.
Keep opening, moving, engaged, garrison and captured populations distinct; do not use live zero displays as numerical evidence.
Broader blockade, occupation and later operations remain campaign context, not additional independent wins or automatic commander credit.
